data.title: Staging
data.tagline: Staging is an isolated pre-production environment used to validate a candidate release under production-like conditions.
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether an environment truly sits before production and name its configuration, data, and access differences from local work and production.
data.description: A candidate version can run in staging with separate services, test payment, and de-identified orders so the team can check a full deployed flow. Staging is one kind of test environment, not a name for every local, CI-ephemeral, or test URL; its defining role is production-like validation before production.

learning.assumes: You know one project can run locally, at a test URL, and at a live URL.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether an environment truly sits before production and name its configuration, data, and access differences from local work and production.

distinctions.label: Deployment
distinctions.explanation: Staging is one kind of target environment used to validate a version. Deployment is the act of placing a version into testing, production, or another environment.

explanation.title: Reproduce key deployment conditions before production
explanation.text: Staging uses a production-like build, configuration, and dependencies to reveal deployed-flow problems, while separate URLs, accounts, and de-identified data protect real users.

explanation.title: The label Staging is not safety proof
explanation.text: Verify the actual version, data connection, keys, external services, and access. An environment named staging but connected to production data is not a safe verification boundary.

data.boundary: Staging is one kind of test environment, not a synonym for every test environment. Local and CI-ephemeral environments can run tests but usually do not provide the production-like, pre-release role of staging. Staging also needs isolation from real users and sensitive data.

lessonPractice.title: The team plans to test “delete order.” Which environment arrangement is safer and gives useful evidence?

options.label: Use test or de-identified orders in isolated staging, confirming the candidate version, production-like configuration, and deletion result
options.feedback: Correct. It tests a production-like full flow without deleting a real customer order.

options.label: Delete one real production order to prove the feature works
options.feedback: A destructive action can affect real users and data and is not ordinary acceptance evidence.

options.label: Only inspect the button on a developer machine, with no data or configuration check
options.feedback: Local appearance does not prove deployed configuration and service connections are right.

data.agentPrompt: Deploy the candidate version to isolated staging and verify order deletion with test or de-identified data. Report the staging URL, running version, production-like configuration, data type, and observable deletion result; do not run destructive testing in production.
